text: Given the first page has more than 100 results, When page_cursor from the response is passed back to offset and the tool is called again, Then there is no parameter validation error, no rejection by Chargebee, and the data immediately following the first page is returned
notes: red->green: before the change, running the same assertion against the real offset:str|None signature is rejected outright at the Pydantic validation stage; after the change 28/28 pass (see the self-test section of docs/tickets/PRD-17977.md)

text: Given the same scenario, When the raw next_offset from the response (instead of page_cursor) is passed back to offset, Then it likewise succeeds - the backward-compatible path
notes: Verifies that the raw next_offset (a 2-element array), after MCP pre-parsing, is passed through directly to Chargebee as list[str] and still works

text: Given the result set is exactly an integer multiple of the page size and more data remains, When pages are turned consecutively until a response has no cursor, Then the accumulated row count matches the total, with no duplicates and no omissions
notes: 3 pages with 5 rows in total, driven page by page with the previous page's page_cursor; the accumulated result matches the expected order exactly

text: Given the result set does not exceed 100 rows, When the tool is called, Then the response body contains no page_cursor / next_offset
notes: When Chargebee returns no next_offset, no cursor field is invented

text: Given a mocked page whose serialized result exceeds 20000 characters, When the tool is called, Then a second request is triggered, and the returned cursor corresponds to the limit of the second request, not the cursor from before truncation
notes: Key red->green case: before the change it directly returned a local slice plus the original cursor (cursor inconsistent with the rows actually returned); after the change the limit of the second request drops from 40 to the safe value computed by fit_count, and the returned next_offset is the second request's own cursor

text: Given offset is passed an unrecognizable/undecodable string, When the tool is called, Then it returns a structured invalid_argument error without raising an uncaught exception
notes: Asserts that no uncaught exception surfaces and that Chargebee was never called (fake_client.calls == [])

text: Given the credentials of two different tenants (different X-Chargebee-Site / X-Chargebee-Api-Key), When a call is made with tenant A's cursor, Then only tenant A's own site data can be fetched, not tenant B's
steps: Prepare credentials for two Chargebee test sites (site A, site B)
Call chargebee_list_subscriptions against site A to get one page of data and a page_cursor
Call again with site A's page_cursor but with the request headers replaced by site B's X-Chargebee-Site / X-Chargebee-Api-Key
Compare which site the data returned by the two calls belongs to
expect: The second call either errors (cursor does not match the current site) or returns site B's own data - it must never return site A's data
notes: Needs credentials for two Chargebee test sites; a production key cannot be used; this machine/round does not have them, environment blocked. TC-CBM-015 already covers the structural guarantee of equal value with a fake client (the cursor carries no tenant information and client_factory resolves per the current request context), but it cannot replace end-to-end verification of Chargebee's real site isolation behavior

text: Given the tool is called without offset, When the response body is checked, Then the original next_offset field still exists and its value is unchanged (relative to the behavior before this change)
notes: Also verifies that the newly added page_cursor field exists and has the correct format

text: Given offset is passed an empty string, When the tool is called, Then it is equivalent to omitting it, returns the first page, and does not error
Given offset is not passed at all, When the tool is called, Then it returns the first page and does not error
notes: Verified separately from TC-CBM-009 for the two 'not provided' input forms

text: Given the Chargebee test site has more than 100 subscriptions, When paging consecutively end to end, Then the complete data set is obtained from the real Chargebee API, rather than the assertion passing through mocks
steps: Prepare a Chargebee test site and make sure the number of subscriptions is > 100
Call chargebee_list_subscriptions with the test site credentials (limit=100, no offset)
After getting page_cursor, call again, and repeat until there is no cursor
Count the accumulated rows and compare with the actual total number of subscriptions in the site back office
expect: The accumulated count matches the actual total in the site back office, with no errors along the way
notes: Needs Chargebee test site credentials and the site needs >100 subscriptions; a production key cannot be used; this round's environment does not have the credentials, environment blocked, not counted as a failure

text: Given the ticket's original scenario is reproduced (Weekly MRR Movement, sopId 281, a period with more than 100 rows), When the agent runs once in the new pagination way, Then it obtains the complete data of that period and no longer stops at row 100
steps: In a test environment, re-run the Weekly MRR Movement agent (sopId 281) in read-only dry-run mode, choosing a period known to have more than 100 rows of Chargebee data
Observe the agent's call trace and returned row counts for chargebee_list_subscriptions/_list_invoices/_list_transactions
Check whether the final report data covers the complete period rather than only the first 100 rows
expect: The report data fully covers all rows of the period, and the agent log shows more than one paginated call, none of which errored
notes: End-to-end regression; needs a test environment + reproducible agent run conditions; this round does not have that environment, environment blocked, not counted as a failure

text: Given offset is passed a valid JSON array string whose content is arbitrarily fabricated (not a value issued by any tool), When the tool is called, Then it returns invalid_argument and is not mistaken for a valid cursor and forwarded to Chargebee
notes: Key red->green case: proves that MCP pre-parsing turns this string into a real list (indistinguishable by type at the Python level from a genuinely passed-back next_offset), so it must be rejected by the shape check in decode_cursor (the first element must be all digits, simulating a Chargebee timestamp cursor) - the assumption of this shape check about Chargebee's real return format has not yet been verified against a real site, see the Risks section of PRD-17977.md

text: Given a cursor issued by another tool is passed to this tool during paging (for example passing the cursor of chargebee_list_invoices to chargebee_list_subscriptions), When the tool is called, Then it returns invalid_argument (cursor does not match the tool/resource), and neither silently returns data of the wrong resource nor crashes
notes: Verifies that the resource tag of encode_cursor/decode_cursor takes effect in the cross-tool scenario

text: Given the same opaque cursor string is sent as-is in a request with another tenant's credentials (simulating cross-tenant replay of that cursor), When the tool is called, Then the site boundary decided by the request headers takes effect, and the data of the site corresponding to the new tenant's credentials is returned (or the cursor is simply invalid under that site and errors), and never the original tenant's site data
notes: Two independent FakeClients simulate two tenants, proving that page_cursor itself carries no tenant information and client_factory resolves per the current request context; the same cursor under another tenant only hits that tenant's own fake client and never reaches the previous tenant's client - this is a structural proof, not end-to-end verification of Chargebee's real site isolation behavior; end-to-end still needs TC-CBM-007
